{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Build on Spring for Apache Kafka (spring-kafka) as the messaging foundation, extending the existing Kafka binder abstraction rather than writing a new client layer.",
    "Implement global configuration options as Spring Boot @ConfigurationProperties defaults, with per-deployment overrides resolved via deployment-level properties (deployment properties take precedence over global defaults).",
    "Map concurrency support to ConcurrentKafkaListenerContainerFactory concurrency for consumers and configurable producer threading/async send options.",
    "Implement compression via Kafka producer compression.type (supporting gzip, snappy, lz4, zstd) with consumer-side transparent decompression.",
    "Implement ACK support through configurable Kafka producer acks settings (0/1/all) and consumer manual acknowledgment mode exposing an Acknowledgment handle so users can confirm successful message/request processing.",
    "Implement the async request-reply pattern using ReplyingKafkaTemplate for bindRequestor (producer expecting async replies) and a @KafkaListener with reply routing (@SendTo / KafkaTemplate send of replies) for bindReplier, correlating request/reply pairs with correlation IDs and dedicated reply topics.",
    "Implement batching through producer batch.size/linger.ms configuration and consumer batch listener support (List of records per poll), with per-deployment override of batch parameters.",
    "Integrate Sqoop via its job execution API; implement job stop by submitting a job abort/kill through the Sqoop/Hadoop job API and releasing allocated connections and resources.",
    "Capture Sqoop logs by attaching a logging appender / redirecting Sqoop client stdout-stderr into the platform SLF4J logging mechanism so logs are streamed to the existing log aggregation.",
    "Implement incremental data load using Sqoop incremental modes (append and lastmodified) with a check-column and persisted last-value stored between runs.",
    "Use Java 17 and Spring Framework 6 / Spring Boot 3 baseline as required; run Kafka acceptance tests against Testcontainers-managed Kafka (with an embedded broker fallback) in the CI pipeline."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "An existing codebase already provides a message-binder abstraction (with at least a basic Kafka binder) and a Sqoop task/job integration skeleton; this increment extends that codebase rather than starting from scratch.",
    "A single developer (the author) performs all work; estimates are pure effort in work-hours, not elapsed duration.",
    "Each feature activity estimate includes its design refinement, implementation, and unit tests; system-level integration/end-to-end testing, documentation, and review/rework are separate activities.",
    "Kafka brokers (via Testcontainers/embedded) and a Hadoop/Sqoop test environment are available for development and CI testing.",
    "No user-interface work is required; all new options are exposed through configuration properties and programmatic APIs.",
    "Documentation scope is limited to configuration reference and developer/usage notes, not full end-user guides.",
    "The developer is experienced with Spring and Kafka; modest ramp-up for Sqoop specifics is included in the Sqoop activity estimates.",
    "Per-deployment override mechanism follows the platform's existing deployment-properties model, so no new override infrastructure needs to be invented.",
    "Estimates assume no major upstream API instability (stable spring-kafka and Sqoop versions)."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Requirements analysis and technical design",
      "activity_description": "Analyze user stories U1-U8, design the global-defaults/per-deployment-override configuration model, the async request-reply design (bindRequestor/bindReplier), the Sqoop stop/logs/incremental-load approach, and produce the implementation plan.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Development environment and CI/test infrastructure setup",
      "activity_description": "Set up Java 17 / Spring Boot 3 build, Testcontainers-managed Kafka for tests, Sqoop/Hadoop test harness access, and the CI pipeline skeleton needed to run acceptance tests on every build.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "U1 - Kafka acceptance test suite with CI integration",
      "activity_description": "Implement acceptance test coverage for Kafka as a message bus (producer/consumer round-trips, binder lifecycle, failure scenarios) and wire the suite into the CI build so it runs on every commit.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "U2 - Concurrency and compression configuration support",
      "activity_description": "Add global default options for consumer/producer concurrency and compression type, with per-deployment override resolution; wire concurrency to the listener container factory and compression to producer configuration; unit tests included.",
      "most_likely_effort": 36
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "U3 - Message acknowledgment (ACK) support",
      "activity_description": "Add configurable producer acks and consumer manual-acknowledgment mode so users can guarantee a sent message/request succeeded; expose acknowledgment API and cover success/failure ack paths with tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "U4 - bindRequestor implementation (producer expecting async replies)",
      "activity_description": "Implement bindRequestor using a replying template: send requests with correlation IDs, manage reply topic subscription, and deliver asynchronous replies to the caller; includes timeouts and unit tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "U4 - bindReplier implementation (consumer handling requests and sending async replies)",
      "activity_description": "Implement bindReplier: consume requests from a requestor topic, invoke the handler, and asynchronously route replies back using correlation IDs and reply topics; includes error handling and unit tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "U5 - Batching support",
      "activity_description": "Add producer batching configuration (batch size, linger) and consumer batch listener support so data can be ingested in batches instead of payload-at-a-time; includes per-deployment overrides and unit tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 28
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "U6 - Stop an existing Sqoop job",
      "activity_description": "Implement the ability to stop a running Sqoop job via the Sqoop/Hadoop job API and clean up allocated resources (connections, temp files, handles) at completion; includes unit tests with a mocked job client.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "U7 - Sqoop log capture and streaming",
      "activity_description": "Investigate and implement capture of Sqoop logs (logging appender and/or stdout-stderr redirection) and stream them into the platform SLF4J logging mechanism for troubleshooting and state evaluation; includes verification tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 36
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "U8 - Incremental data load",
      "activity_description": "Implement Sqoop incremental import support (append and lastmodified modes) with configurable check-column and persisted last-value tracking between runs so only newer rows are retrieved; includes unit tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A12",
      "activity_name": "System integration and end-to-end testing",
      "activity_description": "Perform integration testing across the new features (request-reply over Kafka, batching with concurrency/compression, Sqoop stop/logs/incremental flows), execute full regression, and fix defects found.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A13",
      "activity_name": "Documentation",
      "activity_description": "Document all new configuration options (global defaults and per-deployment overrides), the request-reply binding APIs, ACK semantics, batching, and the Sqoop stop/logs/incremental-load usage.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A14",
      "activity_name": "Code review, rework, and release finalization",
      "activity_description": "Conduct self-review/refactoring, address review findings, finalize CI acceptance-test gating, and prepare the increment for release.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 404
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Build on Spring for Apache Kafka (spring-kafka) as the messaging foundation, extending the existing Kafka binder abstraction rather than writing a new client layer.

Implement global configuration options as Spring Boot @ConfigurationProperties defaults, with per-deployment overrides resolved via deployment-level properties (deployment properties take precedence over global defaults).
Map concurrency support to ConcurrentKafkaListenerContainerFactory concurrency for consumers and configurable producer threading/async send options.
Implement compression via Kafka producer compression.type (supporting gzip, snappy, lz4, zstd) with consumer-side transparent decompression.

Implement ACK support through configurable Kafka producer acks settings (0/1/all) and consumer manual acknowledgment mode exposing an Acknowledgment handle so users can confirm successful message/request processing.

Implement the async request-reply pattern using ReplyingKafkaTemplate for bindRequestor (producer expecting async replies) and a @KafkaListener with reply routing (@SendTo / KafkaTemplate send of replies) for bindReplier, correlating request/reply pairs with correlation IDs and dedicated reply topics.
Implement batching through producer batch.size/linger.ms configuration and consumer batch listener support (List of records per poll), with per-deployment override of batch parameters.
Integrate Sqoop via its job execution API; implement job stop by submitting a job abort/kill through the Sqoop/Hadoop job API and releasing allocated connections and resources.
Capture Sqoop logs by attaching a logging appender / redirecting Sqoop client stdout-stderr into the platform SLF4J logging mechanism so logs are streamed to the existing log aggregation.
Implement incremental data load using Sqoop incremental modes (append and lastmodified) with a check-column and persisted last-value stored between runs.
Use Java 17 and Spring Framework 6 / Spring Boot 3 baseline as required; run Kafka acceptance tests against Testcontainers-managed Kafka (with an embedded broker fallback) in the CI pipeline.
assumptions: An existing codebase already provides a message-binder abstraction (with at least a basic Kafka binder) and a Sqoop task/job integration skeleton; this increment extends that codebase rather than starting from scratch.
A single developer (the author) performs all work; estimates are pure effort in work-hours, not elapsed duration.
Each feature activity estimate includes its design refinement, implementation, and unit tests; system-level integration/end-to-end testing, documentation, and review/rework are separate activities.
Kafka brokers (via Testcontainers/embedded) and a Hadoop/Sqoop test environment are available for development and CI testing.
No user-interface work is required; all new options are exposed through configuration properties and programmatic APIs.
Documentation scope is limited to configuration reference and developer/usage notes, not full end-user guides.
The developer is experienced with Spring and Kafka; modest ramp-up for Sqoop specifics is included in the Sqoop activity estimates.
Per-deployment override mechanism follows the platform's existing deployment-properties model, so no new override infrastructure needs to be invented.
Estimates assume no major upstream API instability (stable spring-kafka and Sqoop versions).
